transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-05 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood CSM); Priya Shah (Atlas Procurement), Evan Li (Atlas Legal), Marcus Reed (Atlas SecOps), Sara Gomez (Atlas ML)

Summary:
Redwood team reviewed MSA exceptions requested by Atlas, discussed DPA clauses, SLA targets and potential credits, and clarified pricing approval path through Atlas procurement committee. Customer wants narrow exceptions for indemnity and data residency plus clarity on on-prem/private deployment options. Agreement on next steps: Redwood to provide redline + executive summary, Security artifacts, and pilot plan for performance/SLA validation.

Topics covered:
- MSA exceptions and negotiation points
- DPA / data handling / residency and KMS requirements
- SLA targets, uptime credits, and service levels for Dedicated/Private options
- Pricing approval timelines and procurement gating
- Pilot scope and acceptance criteria for latency/throughput benchmarks

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: okay thanks everyone for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, I'll kick us off. We have Jordan and Luis on the call as well. Priya, Evan, Marcus, Sara, thanks for making the time.
00:12 Priya Shah: thanks Maya, yeah we wanted to get through the MSA exceptions and make sure we understand the SLA bullets before we go to our procurement board on Friday.
00:20 Maya Chen: for sure. Quick agenda, we'll walk the redline you sent yesterday, focus on the three exception buckets you flagged, then Jordan will talk tech implications for dedicated vs private and what that means for SLA, and then we'll close with next steps.
00:35 Evan Li: just a quick note from legal, we want to keep indemnity language limited and avoid broad third-party IP representations. We also need explicit audit log retention and right to audit for regulated data.
00:47 Jordan Patel: mm-hmm, on the technical side that's doable, the runtime supports audit logs and we can route logs to your SIEM via our secure forwarder, but there are two options — hosted with contractual isolation or Redwood Private in your VPC which gives you full network control.
01:02 Sara Gomez: can you clarify the difference in SLA between hosted and private? I thought private deployments were customer-managed, so Redwood wouldn't commit SLA in the same way, is that correct?
01:12 Jordan Patel: good question. For Redwood Hosted API we provide the standard SLA (99.9 uptime for inference endpoints) with incident credit structure. For Redwood Private — the VPC-managed option — we offer an Enterprise SLA in the contract for availability of the control plane and we can include a runbook for on-call support. If on-prem (air-gapped) there is a different support model and we typically offer a statement of work for installation and an ops SLO rather than the standard hosted SLA.
01:32 Marcus Reed: from SecOps perspective we need details on KMS integration, does Redwood support customer-managed keys/HSM? We'll need to show that to our auditor.
01:40 Maya Chen: yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations — bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for the Private deployment and a managed KMS option for hosted with logical separation. We'll include the KMS diagram in the security package.
01:52 Evan Li: regarding the DPA, there's a clause around data residency and subprocessors. We need confirmation that any logging or metrics forwarded to Redwood systems don't contain PII and that subprocessors list is up to date.
02:05 Luis Ortega: we'll send the current subprocessors list and the DPA template, note that subprocessors are region-aware; for Private deployments subprocessors are minimized, and for Dedicated pools we can control placement.
02:18 Priya Shah: pricing — just to be transparent — our procurement committee wants unit economics for both a pilot and production: per-invocation/token pricing, plus committed capacity pricing. Also need typical onboarding SLAs and estimated ramp timeline.
02:32 Maya Chen: yes, we will provide a pricing sheet with both hosted per-token and a dedicated reserved capacity quote — and an example ramp schedule. We will mark which items need procurement sign-off versus legal sign-off.
02:45 Evan Li: on the MSA exceptions you sent, we have three asks: limit liability cap to 2x fees for the first year, narrow indemnification carveouts for IP, and add an explicit audit and data residency clause. Can you comment?
02:58 Maya Chen: understood. On liability cap, our standard is typically a multiple of annual fees but we'll need to align with our legal team; sometimes we concede to a fixed cap for the first year for enterprise pilots. For IP indemnity, Redwood usually pushes back on broad IP reps but we can add mutual indemnities for third-party claims. For audit and residency we can be explicit about log retention, data deletion, and region scoping in the DPA.
03:20 Evan Li: okay. Can you commit to providing a redline within a week?
03:24 Maya Chen: yes we'll aim to share a redline by Tuesday next week — that's 2026-03-10 — with a one-page summary of major changes for the procurement packet.
03:32 Sara Gomez: technical pilot — we want a 2-week pilot: 100k requests/day, sustained 2k rps peaks for 30s bursts, and sample prompts that reflect our latency-sensitive workflows. We need acceptance criteria for P95 latency under 250ms for short prompts and throughput targets for batch jobs.
03:50 Jordan Patel: thanks, we'll propose a pilot plan. Two options: run in Redwood Dedicated reserved pool (Redwood Dedicated) with guaranteed capacity and a pilot SLA, or spin up a Private trial in your VPC with our control plane and in-region GPUs. Dedicated is faster to stand up; Private gives you more control but a longer setup. For benchmarks, we'll provide a reproducible harness, KV-cache warmup guidance, and recommended sequence lengths.
04:12 Marcus Reed: any logs that leave our VPC in the Private setup? We need assurance that model traces or de-identified telemetry don't contain customer PII.
04:23 Jordan Patel: we have a telemetry pipeline that redacts PII by default, but we'll add a data-flow diagram and show how to opt-out of telemetry. In Private, telemetry can be configured to stay on-prem.
04:36 Priya Shah: procurement gating — our committee meets Friday and they want to see: MSA redline summary, DPA, SOC 2 Type II, and confirmed pricing with a commitment term and exit terms. If we don't get those, approval will be delayed.
04:51 Maya Chen: we hear you. Security artifacts we'll have from our security team by Tuesday, pricing + MSA redline by Tuesday, and a draft SOW for pilot by Thursday. Would that be acceptable?
05:02 Priya Shah: yes that works. One more ask — can you state proposed SLA credits in the MSA redline? Our committee wants concrete numbers, not vague wording.
05:12 Evan Li: specifically they want downtime credit of X% per hour and a mechanism for credit calculation.
05:20 Maya Chen: understood — Jordan, can we offer a sample SLA table with uptime tiers and credit amounts for hosted and dedicated?
05:27 Jordan Patel: yeah we have a default table: 99.9% uptime = 5% credit, 99.5% = 10% credit, below 99% = 25% credit — we can include a separate column for dedicated/private with higher guarantees or SOW-based remedies. Note: percentages and credit mechanics are negotiable by legal.
05:50 Evan Li: also need an escalation path and named contacts for SRE/SE support during the pilot and then for production.
05:58 Luis Ortega: Luis here — CSM will own the day-to-day pilot relationship and provide an escalation matrix; we'll surface on-call SRE contacts for the pilot period in the runbook.
06:10 Sara Gomez: about data deletion — if we need model outputs or embeddings removed, can you confirm retention windows and deletion procedures?
06:19 Jordan Patel: retention is configurable; for hosted we default to 30 days for logs and ephemeral KV caches, but we can shorten that for regulated customers. For embeddings and persistent artifacts we support immediate deletion on request and we'll provide attestation logs.
06:35 Evan Li: subprocessor list and any cross-border transfers — please be explicit.
06:40 Luis Ortega: we'll include the current subprocessor list and region map. For cross-border, for Private deployments there's no cross-region transfer unless requested.
06:50 Priya Shah: one more procurement item — training and knowledge transfer costs. Are those included for the pilot or extra?
06:56 Maya Chen: for basic onboarding and a single enablement session that's included; any deep custom integrations or extended training are typically scoped in an SOW. We'll flag those costs in the pricing sheet.
07:08 Marcus Reed: do you have any references for regulated financial services customers? We prefer seeing a comparable customer who went through onboarding.
07:15 Maya Chen: yes, we'll share anonymized case studies and a reference who completed a Private deployment last year — names and contact will be provided under an NDA if needed.
07:24 Evan Li: about the liability cap — our legal team expects a numeric cap. Will Redwood entertain 2x fees for year one as a pilot concession?
07:32 Maya Chen: I can't promise, but we've done one-year pilot caps before; we'll submit that request to legal and include the proposed wording in the redline.
07:40 Priya Shah: for the MSA exceptions table, can you annotate which items are redlines vs discussion items? makes it easier for our procurement board.
07:47 Maya Chen: yes, the one-pager will have a clear two-column table: exception, Redwood position, proposed language.
07:54 Evan Li: any competitor concerns — our procurement asked if you use any third-party model endpoints like OpenAI or Anthropic as fallbacks, and if so how that is disclosed.
08:06 Jordan Patel: good callout — our model catalog includes open models and we sometimes recommend alternative open checkpoints for cost or latency reasons, but we do not route production requests to third-party API providers without customer consent. We'll add language to the DPA about model sourcing and fallbacks.
08:22 Sara Gomez: timeline — if we get legal + procurement sign-off, how quickly can the pilot start?
08:27 Jordan Patel: Dedicated pilot can start within 7-10 business days after contract execution; Private in-VPC pilot is closer to 3-4 weeks depending on network approvals.
08:36 Priya Shah: okay. Cost approvals — who at Redwood signs off on discounting for a pilot? We have a limited budget for pilots so we might request a small trial discount.
08:46 Maya Chen: pilot discount approvals come from our head of revenue ops; I can include a recommended discount level in the pricing sheet and flag it for internal approval.
08:55 Evan Li: last item from legal — please include a breach notification timeline (we typically expect 72 hours).
09:00 Maya Chen: yes we can commit to a 72-hour notification for confirmed breaches and outline the incident response steps.
09:08 Priya Shah: great. let's outline the concrete deliverables and dates.
09:12 Luis Ortega: action items recap — I'll own the security artifacts delivery, Jordan will own pilot plan, Maya will own MSA redline and pricing.
09:20 Maya Chen: perfect. Any other open questions?
09:25 Marcus Reed: just to confirm — for the pilot performance test, can you provide tooling access or a harness? we prefer something that we can run in our CI to validate latency.
09:33 Jordan Patel: yes we'll provide a reproducible harness and a set of scripts — we'll also provide guidance on KV cache warmup and sequence length distribution matching your workload.
09:45 Priya Shah: one procedural ask — if we accept the MSA exceptions, what's the approval flow inside Redwood for exception acceptance? we want to set expectations on timeline.
09:54 Maya Chen: exceptions require legal review, typically 5-7 business days once we submit a formal request, but for enterprise deals we accelerate to 48-72 hours if it's a small set of limited exceptions and Finance signs off on commercial terms. We'll flag that in the redline summary.
10:09 Evan Li: regarding SLA credits calculation — please put an explicit formula in the redline so we don't have ambiguity.
10:16 Jordan Patel: will do, sample formulas and an example calculation will be in the SLA table.
10:22 Maya Chen: OK, quick recap and next steps: 1) Redwood to send MSA redline + 1-page exceptions summary by 2026-03-10, 2) Security artifacts (SOC2, ISO, subprocessors, KMS diagram) by 2026-03-09, 3) Pilot SOW draft by 2026-03-12, 4) Pricing sheet with pilot discount recommendation by 2026-03-10.
10:46 Priya Shah: that list matches our expectations. We'll aim to route to the procurement committee on Friday subject to receiving docs.
10:53 Maya Chen: great. We'll also include a proposed SLA table with explicit credit mechanics and an escalation matrix in the runbook.
10:59 Evan Li: thanks everyone.
11:02 Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff once legal and procurement greenlight.
11:07 Luis Ortega: thanks, bye.
